## Appearance

Josephine Barry is an elderly woman who appears thin, prim, and rigid. She has a wrinkled cheek and sharp, twinkling black eyes that remain bright and undimmed.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P17](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0017), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P31](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0031), [v1 CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Queen’s P8](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0008)_

## Personality

Josephine Barry is a notably prim and proper elderly woman who is quick to scold others. Additionally, she is described as rather selfish, historically showing little care or concern for anyone besides herself.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P54](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0054), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P31](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0031)_

## History

Josephine Barry, an aunt from [Charlottetown](../codex/places.md#charlottetown), visited [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) and was startled when [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) accidentally leaped onto her in bed. Though initially furious and threatening to cut off Diana's music lessons over the incident, she was amused and charmed by Anne's honest confession. Following their reconciliation, she forgave [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), extended her stay in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), and formed a close friendship with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), later inviting her to visit her in the city.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P27](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0027), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P48](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0048), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. ## Quotes

> "I dare say your claim to sympathy is just as strong as mine. It all depends on the way we look at it. Sit down here and tell me about yourself."
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P88](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0088)

> "Remember, you Anne-girl, when you come to town you’re to visit me and I’ll put you in my very sparest spare-room bed to sleep."
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P96](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0096)

> "Oh, I must, hey? I rather think Diana did her share of the jumping at least. Such carryings on in a respectable house!"
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P82](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0082)

> "She amuses me, and at my time of life an amusing person is a rarity."
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P92](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0092)

> "I’ve made up my mind to stay simply for the sake of getting better acquainted with that Anne-girl,"
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P92](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0092)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--josephine-barry.md)

Josephine Barry and [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) first meet under tense circumstances after [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) accidentally leaps onto Josephine in bed while staying at Diana's house. Driven by remorse, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) visits Josephine to confess her fault directly, where her honesty and charm completely diffuse Josephine's anger and amuse her. From this encounter, the two become firm friends who visit one another, with Josephine ultimately inviting [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to visit her in the city.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P27](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0027), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P48](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0048), [v1 CHAPTER XIX.
